channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: UNDP Constructs 205 Earthquake-Resistant Buildings in Nangarhar with South Korean Aid
item.description: The UNDP has built 205 earthquake-resistant buildings in Nangarhar, Afghanistan, with support from South Korea. The structures include homes and health centers, with 203 housing vulnerable families. The project also created jobs for 719 locals and restored irrigation for 500 acres of farmland.

item.title: Artificial intelligence center for youth established in Balykchy
item.description: An artificial intelligence center for youth has been established in Balykchy, Kyrgyzstan, following a presidential decree. The center, created by "Akademiya IT Star," aims to develop digitalization services export and provide IT training in marketing, programming, and robotics. It has created 100 jobs and offers IT services to over 500 businesses.

item.title: Intensive technologies boost fish farming efficiency in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A fish farming project utilizing intensive technologies has been launched by "Chinobod real biznes" in Balykchy district, Kyrgyzstan. The project, costing 30 billion soms, produces 200 tons of fish meat and 2.5 million fry annually on a two-hectare area. It also includes a laboratory for water purification using chlorella.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva attends UN session, holds meetings in New York
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Presidential Administration of Uzbekistan, attended the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York. She held bilateral meetings with the CEO of the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) to discuss joint projects in transport and healthcare, and with Google's Vice President regarding YouTube monetization.

item.title: Central Asian Experts Discuss Future of Regional Cooperation Amid Global Changes
item.description: An international expert meeting on Central Asia's independent strategies, regional security, and new cooperation formats was held in Cadenabbia, Italy. Organized by the Konrad Adenauer Foundation, the event gathered experts from the region to discuss what shapes Central Asian identity and the future of regional partnerships.

item.title: Balykchy Enterprise Produces Sports Equipment Meeting International Standards
item.description: The 'LB Sport' enterprise in Balykchy, Kyrgyzstan, manufactures sports equipment according to international standards, replacing imports. The project, costing 25 billion soums, produces 65 types of equipment for 18 sports, with an annual output of 500,000 units worth 75 billion soums. Exports reach $3 million annually to Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and CIS countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan actively prepares for the 5th Samarkand Human Rights Forum
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively preparing for the 5th Samarkand Human Rights Forum, scheduled for September 28-29 in Tashkent and Samarkand. The forum will focus on human rights, sustainable development, and international cooperation, marking anniversaries of key human rights pacts and declarations.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Meets Residents and Entrepreneurs on Andijan Gastronomy Street
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev engaged with residents and entrepreneurs on Andijan's gastronomy street in the Orikzor neighborhood. The 1.2-kilometer street created 100 new jobs and can accommodate over 10,000 visitors daily.

item.title: Ucell Showcases Digital Solutions, Including 5G and Energy Infrastructure at ICT Week
item.description: At ICT Week Uzbekistan 2026, Ucell presented digital solutions like 5G, IT infrastructure, and technologies for business and energy. The company highlighted its 5G network, recognized by Ookla, and telecom infrastructure for a 1500 MW wind power plant.

item.title: Two Afghan Citizens Enter US Via Legal Exception to Refugee Policy
item.description: Afghan Evacuate (AfghanIOM) reports two Afghan citizens entered the US through a legal exception to current policies, utilizing the refugee admission program. AfghanIOM's director stated this admission served US national interests. Thousands of Afghans await resettlement.

item.title: Full leather and footwear production cycle established in Altinkul
item.description: A full production cycle for the leather and footwear industry is being created in Altinkul. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the small industrial zone in Andijan region, focusing on deep processing of raw materials and export-oriented production.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev visits ecotourism complex in Asaka
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited an ecotourism complex in Asaka. Once fully operational, the facility is expected to provide 80 billion soums in services annually and contribute 3 billion soums to the local budget.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Dies of Poisoning in Istanbul After Unofficial Treatment
item.description: An Uzbek citizen, Mohirano Meliyeva, died in Istanbul on September 19 due to poisoning from pharmaceutical agents. She was being treated at home by unofficial doctors, which worsened her condition. Despite being taken to hospital, doctors could not save her life. Her body was repatriated.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Reviews Xinjiang Cotton Growing Method Using Drip Irrigation
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed the Xinjiang method of cotton cultivation, which uses drip irrigation and fertilization systems to deliver water and nutrients directly to the plant roots. This method reportedly saves up to 40% of water and nearly 30% of fertilizer.

item.title: Bishkek Residents Learn About Eco-Friendly Heating Systems
item.description: An informational meeting was held in Bishkek for residents interested in eco-friendly and energy-efficient heating systems, specifically heat pumps. Participants learned about preferential state loans for installation, equipment costs, and operational benefits, including during electricity supply restrictions. The project is supported by the World Bank.

item.title: US, Denmark, and Greenland sign defense agreement to expand US military presence
item.description: The US, Denmark, and Greenland have signed a security agreement allowing the US to expand its military presence on the island. The deal amends a 1951 defense treaty and could lead to two additional US military bases.

item.title: Smart water meters production launched in Khodjaabad technopark
item.description: Production of smart water meters has been launched at the Khodjaabad technopark in Uzbekistan's Andijan region. The project, a joint venture with Chinese company Sanchuan and support from Huawei, aims for precise water consumption control.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Kochkor District Still Addressing Aftermath of July Mudflows
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Emergency Situations visited Kochkor district in Naryn region to assess the consequences of July mudflows. Four out of five affected state railway sections are cleared, with plans for protective measures on the remaining one and a new mudflow channel.

item.title: Iranian President: We are not afraid of war, nor do we shy away from negotiation
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated at the UN General Assembly that Iran is not afraid of war for self-defense and does not avoid negotiation for peace. He asserted that threats strengthen the Iranian nation and that they will not accept the language of force.

item.title: Journalist's Trial in Bishkek Postponed Due to Absent Experts
item.description: A Bishkek court postponed the retrial of journalist Makhabat Tajibek kyzy because key experts failed to appear. Defense questioned an expert's competence, while the prosecution cited language day events and illness. The case relates to media projects Temirov LIVE and Ait, Ait.

item.title: Uzbekistan Ranks First in CIS for Wired Internet Speed
item.description: Uzbekistan has achieved the top position in the CIS for wired internet speed, attributed to years of network modernization efforts. This involved collaboration among communication operators, internet providers, and the main infrastructure provider, Uztelecom.

item.title: Women's Rights Advocates Warn of Entrenched Taliban Rule and Normalization
item.description: Afghan women's rights advocates in New York expressed concern that Taliban rule and restrictions on women are becoming entrenched. They warned that international engagement risks normalizing these policies, potentially requiring decades to reverse such institutionalized changes.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev Visits Artificial Intelligence Center in Baliqchi
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the Artificial Intelligence center in Baliqchi. The head of state familiarized himself with startups created by young people, highly praising their knowledge and intellectual potential. He engaged with the young innovators.

item.title: Pakistan urges OIC to press Taliban on militant groups and women's rights
item.description: Pakistan's foreign minister called on the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) to pressure the Taliban to dismantle militant groups operating in Afghanistan and end their alleged support. Speaking at an OIC meeting, he urged the group to encourage the Taliban to combat terrorism and comply with international obligations, noting that attacks against Pakistan originate from Afghanistan.

item.title: Navoiyuran State Enterprise Holds Open Meeting with Media on Compliance and Geology
item.description: The Navoiyuran State Enterprise in Uzbekistan held an open meeting with media representatives to discuss its work, results, and tasks. Key topics included anti-corruption measures, compliance systems, geological exploration, and occupational safety, fostering transparency and dialogue.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Cultural Heritage Agency Criticized Over Protection Priorities
item.description: Party chairman Alisher Qodirov criticized Uzbekistan's Cultural Heritage Agency for prioritizing Soviet-era structures over historical monuments. He highlighted an 11th-century building near a ziyarat site, whose preservation is stalled due to funding and new burials. The agency previously stated cultural heritage has no nationality.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enacts Law Mandating Closed Hearings for Juvenile Criminal Cases
item.description: A new Uzbek law, effective September 12, 2026, mandates that criminal cases involving minors will only be heard in closed sessions. This amendment to the Criminal Procedure Code aims to protect minors' privacy, aligning national legislation with international standards on child protection and preventing negative impacts from public trials.

item.title: Pakistan claims drone attacks originate from Afghanistan; Kabul responds
item.description: A report discusses claims by Pakistan regarding drone attacks allegedly originating from Afghanistan and Kabul's response to these accusations. The segment features a discussion with Shah Mahmood Miakhil, former acting minister and first deputy minister of the National Defense Ministry in the previous government, analyzing the situation.

item.title: Andijan Launches 206 New Investment Projects Worth $9.4 Billion
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended the launch ceremony for 206 new investment projects in Andijan region, totaling $9.4 billion. Of these, 98 projects worth $2.05 billion are operational, while 108 projects worth $7.35 billion have begun construction. These initiatives span energy, construction, textiles, and more.

item.title: Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, and Turkey Begin Joint Military Exercises 'Unity Strength 2026'
item.description: Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, and Turkey have commenced joint military exercises named 'Unity Strength 2026' in Azerbaijan. The drills involve military personnel, equipment, aviation, and drones, focusing on enhancing interoperability and experience exchange. The exercises will be conducted in three phases across various Azerbaijani training grounds.

item.title: Tajikistan Mandates HIV Testing for Beauty Salon Staff and Newlyweds
item.description: Tajikistan has implemented a new government decree requiring mandatory HIV testing for beauty salon employees and newlyweds. Those diagnosed with the virus will be prohibited from working in the beauty industry. This requirement was not present in previous regulations and aims to control the spread of infections.

item.title: Russia Expresses Concern Over Civilian Casualties in Eastern Afghanistan Airstrikes
item.description: The Russian Embassy in Kabul voiced concern over civilian deaths from airstrikes in eastern Afghanistan, without naming Pakistan. The embassy expressed sympathy to victims' families and urged all parties to avoid confrontation and resolve disputes through dialogue. Pakistan's army had previously bombed targets in Kunar and Paktika provinces.

item.title: UK Ministry of Defence Discovers 97 Million Documents Potentially Relevant to Afghan War Crimes Probe
item.description: The UK Ministry of Defence has found 97 million new documents that could be relevant to an investigation into alleged civilian killings by special forces in Afghanistan. The inquiry head expressed concern that the late discovery of these documents might significantly delay the ongoing investigation.

item.title: Qatar Ready to Host Fourth Doha Meeting on Afghanistan, Foreign Ministry States
item.description: Qatar is prepared to host the fourth meeting of special envoys on Afghanistan, according to its Foreign Ministry. The statement came during the OIC Contact Group meeting on Afghanistan on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. Qatar has previously hosted similar dialogues.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey to Expand Cooperation in Legal Information Sphere
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkey plan to enhance collaboration in legal information exchange, focusing on digitalization of legislative databases and adoption of modern technologies. A recent visit by a Turkish delegation to Uzbekistan's 'Adolat' center facilitated discussions on sharing experiences and developing joint digital solutions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Seizes Over 1.4 Tons of Drugs in Eight Months
item.description: In Uzbekistan, over 12,000 drug-related crimes were detected in the first eight months of the year. During this period, 89 major drug trafficking groups were dismantled. Authorities confiscated 1.4 tons of traditional drugs and 61.7 kg of synthetic substances.

item.title: Russian Tour Operators Report Increased Demand for Uzbekistan Travel
item.description: Russian tour operators have noted a significant rise in demand for tours to Uzbekistan this autumn, with sales up to 65% compared to last year. Classic excursion routes and short city tours are most popular. Increased flight connections are cited as a contributing factor.

item.title: Afghan Air Force Denies Pakistani Claims of Drone Strikes
item.description: An Afghan source has refuted Pakistani security officials' claims of sending drones into Pakistan. The Afghan Air Force has not conducted any drone attacks, and the Islamic Emirate will determine the timing and nature of any retaliatory response.

item.title: Taliban Intelligence Detains Two Police Officers in Panjshir
item.description: Taliban intelligence in Panjshir province has reportedly arrested two local police officers, identified as 'Dr. Faiz' and 'Matiullah'. Both were previously employed by the previous government and worked in the Panjshir security command. The reason for their detention remains unclear.

item.title: Taliban Report 15 Deaths from Well Falls in Past Year
item.description: Afghanistan's National Disaster Management Authority reported 24 incidents of falling into water wells over the past year, resulting in 15 deaths, including 11 children. Nine individuals were rescued. A special rescue team has been formed to address such incidents.
